key_insight: Bosonic cyclic codes trade a small amount of loss-detection capability for many passive, Gaussian-implementable logical phase gates, extending rotation-symmetric bosonic codes beyond a single logical Pauli.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware-efficient bosonic qubits a tunable path toward fault-tolerant control, improving the practicality of quantum error correction for computation.
method: Generalize rotation-symmetric bosonic codes into cyclic codes with measured symmetry breaking.
Construct cyclic cat and Vandermonde code families as bosonic analogs of cat and binomial codes.
Use higher-order $SU(2)$/rotation symmetries to derive extra stabilizers, Pauli gates, and non-Clifford operations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that sacrificing detectability of a single photon loss can produce a number of logical phase gates commensurate with the code’s rotation symmetry order, all achievable via passive Gaussian rotations.
watch_item: The gate-enhancement comes with reduced photon-loss detectability, so the performance tradeoff must be carefully benchmarked against physical noise and control imperfections.
paper_title: Bosonic Cyclic Codes: Trading Stabilizers for Gaussian Non-Clifford Phase Gates
